A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Hoi! dataset and contain readable main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices. Retained material can be matched despite reformatting and appendix renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original trajectory-accuracy, articulation-estimation, tactile-force, visual-force, and hand-pose evaluations, including results in its appendix.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical evaluations and adds original Spot manipulation experiments using a force predictor trained on Hoi! data.

M1.justification: New Appendix D.4 introduces a learning-and-control procedure absent from v2: frozen DINOv2 features and an MLP predict a residual around a class-specific log-force prior, trained against peak interaction forces. The predicted force becomes a feed-forward term in Spot's controller. This substantially extends the methodology beyond the retained capture pipeline and perception benchmarks.

E1.justification: v3 adds learned robotic manipulation evaluated through successful operation of a drawer, oven, and dishwasher in the lab. This introduces an action-execution task beyond v2's perception evaluations and teleoperated Spot recordings. The underlying 3048-sequence, 381-object, 38-environment dataset remains unchanged.

E2.justification: Appendix D.4 adds standard impedance control, labeled Position in the results, as a comparator to the controller augmented with predicted force. The existing ArtGS, ArtiPoint, GPT-5, Sparsh, ForceSight, and hand-pose comparisons retain their comparator membership.

E3.justification: The new robot evaluation introduces success rate, initialization in front of each object, and a handle-position heuristic controlling articulation-type selection. Table 4 also replaces P-labeled type scores with explicitly identified recall R and corrects motion-error column definitions. These reporting revisions do not establish that the existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Appendix D.4 adds a component comparison testing control with versus without the learned feed-forward force term across objects with differing mechanical stiffness. Existing gravity-compensation illustrations, tactile underprediction analysis, raw-versus-projected force comparison, and exploratory hand-pose analysis are retained.

E5.justification: The new robot experiment reports five operations per articulated part, adding explicit repeated-trial information. It supplies no confidence intervals or training-seed statistics. Existing tactile-force 95% confidence intervals and temporal-alignment uncertainty reporting are unchanged.

E6.justification: v3 adds robot success rates of 100/0/0% for Position versus 100/80/60% for Position-Force on drawer/oven/dishwasher, plus average predicted forces of 16.80/46.38/53.29 N. Table 4 changes all three GPT-5 rows; Hoi! egocentric values change from 88.5/74.3 to 71.9/89.7 under the revised recall labeling, so these are not established same-metric performance changes. Other retained benchmark results are unchanged.

T1.justification: Appendix D.4 adds mathematical definitions of the residual log-force predictor, squared regression objective, and baseline and augmented control laws in Equations 2–5. Existing calibration, alignment, and force-decomposition mathematics remains unchanged; no new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: the multimodal capture pipeline, Hoi! dataset, and interaction annotations supporting cross-view and cross-embodiment research. The new robot experiment adds supporting evidence without materially redefining these core claims.

C2.justification: Appendix D.4 newly interprets the controller results as evidence that learned force priors improve real-world manipulation and demonstrate Hoi!'s potential for multimodal policy learning. It also explains the articulation heuristic as reducing misclassification confounds. Existing benchmark interpretations and Section 5 limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: New Appendix A.1 and Supplementary Table 7 disclose sensor fields of view, resolutions, recording rates, and force–torque accuracy and noise specifications. D.4 documents backbone freezing and the force-target transformation. These additions do not establish changes to existing acquisition settings. The project website link remains the same.

R1.justification: Both versions cite the same 55 bibliography entries and retain the same substantive positioning relative to articulation, video-understanding, and manipulation datasets. Bibliographic formatting and removal of citation back-reference page numbers do not change research positioning.

P1.justification: v3 lightly edits and shortens the abstract and introduction, adds Funding & Acknowledgments, and expands the appendix organization with sensor specifications and robot learning. Hand Pose Estimation moves from D.4 to D.5. The existing narrative and most explanatory prose are retained.

P2.justification: The document is retypeset throughout, changing typography, heading and caption styles, figure scaling, and float placement. The appendix regroups the gravity-compensation and alignment figures. v3 also adds sensor-specification and controller-results tables and revises Table 4's headers and caption; existing figure content is largely retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides useful direct evidence connecting Hoi!-trained force prediction to robot manipulation, whereas v2 primarily demonstrated perception benchmarks. Sensor specifications improve reproducibility, and Table 4's corrected error-column labels improve interpretability. The gain remains limited: the robot study uses five operations per part and omits training splits, key hyperparameters, and uncertainty estimates, so it supports an illustrative demonstration rather than broad generalization.
